## Introduction

This short report looks at **highway fuel economy** in the `mpg` data that
comes with the tidyverse. It shows the parts of a Quarto document: a header,
text, and code chunks.

## Data

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
```

Each row of `mpg` is one model of car. We use `hwy` (highway miles per gallon)
and `displ` (engine size in liters).

```{r}
#| label: glimpse
glimpse(mpg)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: cutoff
cutoff <- 30
n_above <- sum(mpg$hwy > cutoff)
share_above <- mean(mpg$hwy > cutoff)
```

In these data, `r n_above` of `r nrow(mpg)` models get more than `r cutoff`
highway miles per gallon (`r round(100 * share_above, 1)`%).

## A graphic

```{r}
#| label: fig-hwy
#| fig-cap: "Larger engines tend to get fewer highway miles per gallon."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Engine displacement (liters)",
       y = "Highway mileage (mpg)",
       caption = "Source: mpg data frame in ggplot2")
```

@fig-hwy shows the pattern. This is a pattern in these cars, and it does not
tell us that engine size causes the difference.
